text:
marta: quick follow-up from the FlashAttention RFC — after enabling v3 by default in the kernel selector we observed p99 latency regressions for long contexts (6k-8k) on H100 nodes. opening thread to capture root causes and next steps.

ajay: can you paste the microbench numbers and the selector config you used?

marta: yea, ran the bench with our standard harness (batching disabled, streaming). results below (tokens/sec, lower is worse):
```
H100, seq=8192, batch=1: native=4200, flashv2=4800, flashv3=3700
H100, seq=4096, batch=2: native=7600, flashv2=8200, flashv3=8100
A100, seq=8192, batch=1: native=4000, flashv2=4500, flashv3=4400
```
selector config snippet: 
```
kernel_selector:
  prefer_flashv3: true
  flashv3_min_seq: 512
  flashv3_max_batch: 16
  fallback_order: [native, flashv2]
```
Note: flashv3 was picked for the 8k run and we saw a 10-15% p99 regress vs flashv2.

lucy: interesting — did you enable workspace pooling? flashv3 allocs a larger workspace and our allocator currently does per-request cudaMalloc when pool miss happens. that can blow up p99 for single-request large seq.

marta: good call — workspace_pooling: enabled, but pool hit rate was ~72% on the bench. the misses lined up with the highest p99 spikes.

zane: two quick ideas: 1) add a small per-device preallocated splat for the largest workspace to avoid malloc on cold path, 2) adjust selector to bias against flashv3 when pool hit < 90% for that seq/batch shape.

ajay: +1. also worth checking memory fragmentation — we saw fragmentation creeping after long runs (stability infra test), which would reduce pool hits. can we add pool telemetry (alloc_count, hit_rate, fragmentation_estimate) to the console?

infra-bot: benchmark-runner finished: https://ci.internal/bench/1767500000 — full logs and perf traces attached.

marta: i opened a small PR to change the selector thresholds and add a pool-miss guard: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/2127 (draft). core change is: if expected_pool_hit(seq,batch,device) < 0.9 then prefer flashv2/native.

lucy: can you also try toggling the workspace defrag heuristic? adding a periodic defrag reduced fragmentation in my local stress runs. small config: `workspace_defrag_interval=600s`.

marta: will try — initial runs look promising: p99 improved ~12% when we force prealloc for the 8k workspace. i'll post numbers.

azaj: (typo) ajay: i meant to say we should also export kernel selection decisions in trace spans so we can correlate selector choices with p99 spikes.

ajay: yes, trace + metric. metric: selector_chosen{kernel,device,seq,batch} increment on decision. trace: include reason code (pool_hit, mem_pressure, heuristic).

zane: long-term thought: selector should be occupancy-aware. flashv3 has different occupancy and register usage on H100 vs A100. maybe query device compute capability and use a small LUT mapping (seq,batch,device)->expected_tokens_per_sec from offline bench. cheaper than heuristics.

lucy: agree, we already have per-model perf profiles for compilation choices. reusing that infra makes sense.

marta: action items: 1) (marta) land pool prealloc + pool-miss guard in selector (PR 2127), 2) (lucy) add defrag toggle and run stress test, 3) (ajay) add selector metric & trace spans, 4) (zane) prototype per-device perf LUT and run automated calibration. i'll update this thread with new bench runs. :+1:

marta: one more note — observed weird numeric differences with flashv3 quant kernels on fp16 edgecases (low-value tokens) — need to file a small correctness test. not blocking but logging it.

ajay: file an issue, mark as low severity but add a regression-eval to the CI prompt-set.

marta: filed: https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/879 — thanks everyone.

(threads tend to be short replies, but this one captures the important follow-up items)
